TL;DR — root cause appears to be a quota-window mismatch combined with an aggressive burst limiter.

Details:
- What I see in metrics (attached quota-metrics-20270210.csv): Brightline's traffic pattern includes many short bursts (hundreds of small requests in <30s) rather than sustained long requests.
- Our quota token-window was configured at 60s with a small refill quantum due to a recent optimization for other customers. That policy treats rapid-fire short requests as exceeding the window even when average QPS is within committed capacity.
- The burst limiter then kicked in and started returning 429s; clients retried aggressively which increased load and produced a handful of 5xx from backpressure cascades.

Immediate mitigations (proposed):
1) Temporarily widen the quota window from 60s -> 180s for Brightline's route and increase burst cap by 3x. This should absorb short spikes without violating their committed rate.
2) Route tolerant/low-priority requests to a degraded model variant while preserving latency-sensitive routes.
3) Add a short client-side guidance note to Brightline: backoff jitter and prefer longer polling intervals for batch calls.

I can apply (1) now as a scoped, per-account override. We should also schedule a follow-up to tune production token refill size and add monitoring alerts for quota-window saturation.
